messages.author: 823dbccdc15c7f4a
messages.subject: multiple alpha values: bug?
parts:
Hi,
is this a bug? When I specify the alpha value with a function it only works correctly when both have the same value. When one of them is different the higher one seems to be always displayed with alpha=1.
In other words:

df <- data.frame(x=1:10,y=1:10,s=c(T,F))

#both are transparent:
ggplot(df, aes(x=x,y=y,colour=s)) + geom_point(aes(alpha=ifelse(s,0.2, 0.2)))

#suddenly the green looses transparency (but it should be 0.6)
ggplot(df, aes(x=x,y=y,colour=s)) + geom_point(aes(alpha=ifelse(s,0.3, 0.2)))

#this is how 0.3 looks like:
ggplot(df, aes(x=x,y=y,colour=s)) + geom_point(aes(alpha=ifelse(s,0.3, 0.3)))

#now the orange is solid!
ggplot(df, aes(x=x,y=y,colour=s)) + geom_point(aes(alpha=ifelse(s,0.2, 0.3)))

ggplot(df, aes(x=x,y=y,colour=s)) + geom_point()

best,
ido

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: multiple alpha values: bug?
parts:
You seem to be assuming that the alpha values should be equal to the
values of the variable to which alpha is mapped. That is generally
incorrect; the alpha values are determined by the alpha scale. You can
use an alpha scale that does set the alpha as you expected;

ggplot(df, aes(x=x,y=y,colour=s)) + geom_point(aes(alpha=ifelse(s,0.3, 0.2))) +
scale_alpha_identity(guide = "legend")

but this is not the default; you have to ask for it.

Best,
Ista

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: multiple alpha values: bug?
parts:
On 8 January 2014 14:27, ido <IdoM...@gmail.com> wrote:
Wouldn't it make sense to always have a default identity for each scale?

Input data can be in any range, say [1e-9, 1e-2] -- you wouldn't want that as a default point size. Default scales map to a range of rendering parameters in the graphic space that will be clearly visible and distinguishable on a piece of paper.

b.
